text: dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard 是面向 DSH Web 的侧栏迷你仪表盘，在设置项上方显示可拖动、可调整大小的悬浮面板。它汇总活跃及今日会话、今日输入输出与缓存 token、实时吞吐速度，并显示当前会话的 Git 分支和工作区变更。用户可切换紧凑、卡片或列表布局，调整刷新频率、显示指标、趋势线与外观；今日用量按本地日统计，流式生成时估算输出速度。配置保存在 DSH 设置中，不需要额外密钥或外部账号。

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard adds a draggable, resizable DSH Web dashboard for active sessions, daily token use, live throughput, and current-session Git status. Choose compact, card, or list layout; adjust metrics, refresh, trends, and appearance. Settings stay in DSH; no API key is needed.
想在 DSH 网页侧栏旁快速查看当前有多少会话正在运行。
能不能把今天的 token 输入、输出和缓存用量放在一个小面板里？
我想实时看模型每秒输入和输出多少 token。
希望直接从 DSH 面板看当前项目的 Git 分支和改动量。
Show my active sessions and today’s token usage in a small DSH Web panel.
I want a live view of token throughput and Git changes for the current session.
想把仪表盘改成列表或紧凑布局，并隐藏不关心的统计项。
Can I keep a small resizable dashboard visible while working in DSH Web?
**dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard** 的功能「会话概览」：汇总当前活跃会话和今日有活动的会话数量；活跃状态也考虑正在运行的子代理。
**dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard** 的功能「今日用量」：按本地自然日汇总输入、输出及缓存读写 token；可选择是否计入子代理会话。
**dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard** 的功能「实时吞吐」：通过用量采样显示输入和输出速度；回复流式生成期间根据可见文本估算输出速度。
**dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard** 的功能「Git 工作区状态」：显示当前会话工作目录的分支、变更文件数和增删行数；端点按需推送状态更新。
**dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard** 的功能「悬浮面板与趋势」：提供紧凑、卡片和列表布局，可拖动及调整大小，并为速度指标显示可选趋势线。
dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard 使用前须知：Git 指标读取当前会话工作目录的本地分支和改动状态；Git 不可用时显示为空状态。

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard：A session & token mini dashboard for DSH web. It renders just above the sidebar's "Settings" row and summarizes, in one small draggable float window, what your sessions are doing right now and what they have cost you today.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/focksor/dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard)

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · What it shows：| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Active sessions | Sessions running right now — including ones busy through a running subagent. Counted exactly like the sidebar status lights, so the number always matches the sidebar. |
| Today | Sessions with activity today; blank sessions never count. |
| In/s · Out/s | Current token throughput (tokens/s), decaying naturally to zero when idle. Scope is configurable: all sessions, or just the one you are working in. While a reply is still streaming and the provider has not reported usage yet, output speed is estimated live from the streamed text (≈ 4 characters per token); the larger of the two figures is shown. |
| In · Out | Tokens sent and generated today. |
| Cache read · Cache write | Today's cached-token usage, shown as two independently toggleable metrics. |
| Branch | Current git branch of the current session's working directory (detached HEAD shows `HEAD`; upstream tracking/ahead info is stripped). |
| Changes | Working-tree changes vs HEAD: changed file count from `git status` (untracked files included, renames count once) plus `+added -removed` line sums from `git diff HEAD --numstat`

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · What it shows：**Git metrics** — the three git rows follow the **current session's** working directory and stream over an SSE endpoint the plugin mounts at `/mini-dashboard/events` (same `webServer.register` mechanism as the in-box client-hmr channel). The endpoint accepts session ids only — never paths — and unknown ids answer 404; it sends no CORS headers and relies on DSH web's default posture of a loopback-bound, auth-free web surface. When git or the endpoint is unavailable the cells show `—`, polling follows the panel's refresh interval (clamped to 1–30s by the endpoint), and the stream is closed only when all three git metrics are hidden or the panel is disabled — any single hidden metric keeps the stream open, since the three share one connection. An empty repository still names its branch, with the line counts reading 0 (nothing to diff against HEAD yet). All three are shown by default and can be toggled individually in Visible metrics; trendlines remain speed-metric-only.

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · What it shows：**Speed trendlines** — both speed metrics can show a small sparkline next to the value: a filled curve along the card's right edge in Cards layout, a thin curve under the row in List layout, none in Compact. Pick Off / 1m / 3m / 5m per metric (default: 5 minutes for both). History is kept in memory for about 6 minutes and starts fresh after a page refresh; its detail follows the refresh interval.

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · The float window：- Drag it by the header; resize from the bottom, right or corner edges. The height hugs the content until you fix one yourself — a fixed height is then shared evenly by the metrics, scrolling if it gets too short.
- First launch places it at the bottom-right; position and size are remembered across restarts.
- It snaps to screen edges when dropped nearby (threshold adjustable).
- Content and backdrop transparency sliders let it blend into your theme; light and dark are handled automatically.
- It stays above host dialogs and dropdowns, and hides itself while the sidebar is collapsed to the narrow rail.
- With every metric turned off, only the title and the ⚙ button remain.
- Running several DSH web windows at once? They share one saved position, and each window keeps the panel fully inside its own viewport — a spot dragged out in a big window stays visible in a small one. The last window you move it in wins.

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard
```

Restart `dsh web` to take effect.

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · Configuration：Two places edit the same settings, and every change applies instantly:

1. the **mini dashboard** section in DSH's built-in Settings dialog;
2. the **⚙ popover** on the panel itself — same options, always one click away.

Settings persist to `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` (namespace `mini-dashboard`) and survive restarts.

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · Configuration：| Setting | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enable panel | on | Master switch |
| Layout | Cards | Compact single row / Cards grid / List rows |
| Refresh interval | 2s | Update cadence (1/2/5/10/30s); also caps trendline detail |
| Speed scope | Current session | Count speeds across all sessions or the current one only |
| Output speed includes reasoning | on | On: 10s window, thinking text counts toward the live estimate. Off: smoother 30s window that ignores it |
| Today usage includes subagents | on | Whether subagent sessions add to today's token figures |
| Columns per row | 2 | Card layout density (1–4) |
| Snap to screen edge | on | Magnet when dragging near an edge; a threshold slider (8–80px) appears alongside |
| Fg / Bg transparency | 0% / 15% | Fade the metric text / the backdrop |
| Visible metrics | all shown | Per-metric show/hide; drag to reorder |
| Trendline | 5m (both speeds) | Off / 1m / 3m / 5m, set per speed metric |
| Git metrics | shown | Branch / Changes / combined Git status, each individually toggleable in Visible metrics |

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · How the numbers are counted：- Session counts (Active, Today) mirror the sidebar: blank, archived and subagent-origin rows are never counted. A session counts as active when it is running itself, or when a subagent behind it is running.
- Today's token figures are true per-day totals: provider usage is bucketed into 30-minute slots and summed over your local day. Archived sessions still count — tokens already spent do not disappear when a session is archived.
- Cold sessions (not loaded in this host run) are served from DSH's persisted projection cache, which only holds rows written while the plugin was active. To close that gap the plugin backfills the cache at startup: every persisted session with activity inside the projection retention window gets its usage re-folded to the end of its log via the host's cold-read ladder, and the panel nudges one full session-list refresh until every visible row carries the projection — so the totals include all of today's sessions, not just the ones opened since the plugin came up.

dsh-plugin-mini-dashboard README · Language：The panel follows DSH's language setting (Settings → Language) with Chinese and English text, switching instantly — no refresh needed.
